projects.name: Qualcomm ELD Contributions
projects.summary: Four merged fixes in Qualcomm's LLVM-based ELF linker across GNU option compatibility, header layout, native LTO output, and linker-script diagnostics.
projects.flow: Object files + linker script → symbol and section layout → ELF executable
features: Accepted numeric GNU -O compatibility options while keeping LTO optimization controls independent.
Guarded ELF/program-header address assignment when a linker script omits those headers from the output layout.
Preserved native ARM/AArch64 object emission with --save-temps, covering full LTO, ThinLTO, and explicit assembly output.
Added source line numbers to duplicate PROVIDE and PROVIDE_HIDDEN warnings so diagnostics identify the exact assignment.
Reproduced failures and added regression coverage for x86-64, Hexagon, ARM, AArch64, RV32, and RV64 configurations.
projects.notes: Four PRs are merged as of 30 October 2026. Focused regression validation covered six target configurations; the full ELD suite was not run. AArch64 feature-flag and contributor-documentation changes remain open.
highlights: GNU numeric -O compatibility with independent LTO optimization controls.
PHDRS/FILEHDR crash fix and native ARM/AArch64 LTO saved objects.
Precise PROVIDE warning locations; focused regressions across 6 target configurations.

contributions.title: #2011 · GNU numeric -O compatibility
contributions.detail: Unblocked warning-sensitive Meson links while leaving --lto-O controls independent. Regression coverage across six target configurations.

contributions.title: #2065 · PHDRS/FILEHDR layout crash
contributions.detail: Guarded header address assignment when a linker script omits headers from the output layout; checked both header combinations.

contributions.title: #2129 · Native LTO saved objects
contributions.detail: Preserved native ARM/AArch64 object emission with --save-temps; covered full LTO, ThinLTO, and explicit assembly output.

contributions.title: #2207 · Linker-script warning locations
contributions.detail: Included source line numbers in duplicate PROVIDE and PROVIDE_HIDDEN warnings; both updated regressions passed across six target configurations.

contributions.title: #2134 · AArch64 feature flags
contributions.detail: Preserved BTI/PAC flags across multiple sections in one input. The regression failed before the fix; 18 focused runs passed after it.

contributions.title: #2127 · Contributor build guidance
contributions.detail: Documented LLVM main alignment and space-free source/build paths following hands-on WSL setup and maintainer discussion.

projects.name: Legal Lens 2.0
projects.summary: Contributed hybrid retrieval and a cited research assistant that connects legal questions to page-level evidence.
projects.flow: PDF pages → BM25 + MiniLM indexes → reciprocal rank fusion → cited answer or source excerpts
features: Combined lexical and semantic ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, keeping PDF page references attached to retrieved passages.
Added retrieval-augmented generation with page-linked citations and a document-excerpt fallback when generation is unavailable.
Implemented local scope/intent classification using MiniLM embeddings and logistic regression, plus cited research-brief export.
projects.notes: Historical source corpus; current-law coverage is unverified. The evaluation is a small, author-created pilot, not a representative or expert-reviewed benchmark. A labelled passage hit does not establish answer accuracy. See the evaluation branch report for methodology, failures, fallback handling, and local warm timings.
highlights: BM25 + MiniLM with reciprocal rank fusion over a 1,871-page historical IPC source.
Cited answers, excerpt fallback, local intent classification, and research-brief export.
Author-created pilot: BM25 and hybrid each found labelled passages in the top 5 for 14 of 27 historical questions; 8 of 8 scope cases returned no evidence.

projects.name: Signal · Recommendation Lab
projects.summary: An interactive recommendation lab that makes collaborative filtering visible, explainable, and fun to explore.
projects.flow: Fictional ratings → user/item similarity or popularity → ranked suggestions → evidence and held-out evaluation.
features: Change listener ratings and see recommendations and before-and-after predictions update immediately.
Compare user-based, item-based and regularized popularity methods; inspect neighbor similarity and clearly labelled cold-start fallbacks.
Run leave-one-rating-out MAE and direct-coverage comparisons on the same small synthetic dataset.
Preserves the original coursework notebook on review analysis and collaborative filtering.
projects.notes: A learning demo built on fictional products and ratings, not an evaluation of the original Amazon dataset or a production recommender. The historical notebook relies on external data and its results have not been independently reproduced.
highlights: Three recommendation strategies, live rating controls, and transparent neighbor evidence.
Interactive holdout evaluation, cold-start fallback, and before-and-after predictions.

projects.name: Real Estate Aggregator
projects.summary: A property marketplace prototype exploring searchable listings, account workflows, and contracts, with a safe synthetic preview.
projects.flow: PHP/Slim routes → account and property workflows → MySQL, email and PDF integrations; payment routes disabled.
features: Built listing creation/editing and filters for location, budget, availability, and amenities.
Added deny-before-dispatch authorization and bound parameters for listing filters, with focused regression checks.
Retained legacy payment integration for study; payment endpoints are disabled pending transaction and security work.
projects.notes: Prototype only. The standalone preview uses fictional listings and no accounts or payments. Payment endpoints are disabled; database, identity, upload and authorization paths still need broader review.
highlights: Searchable property listings with account workflows and parameterized filters.
Synthetic preview; payment routes disabled pending transaction and security work.

projects.name: GPT-2 Review Summarization
projects.summary: Coursework experiment in review summarization, now paired with a corrected, reproducible evaluation.
projects.flow: Reviews → preprocessing and split → GPT-2 fine-tuning → checkpoint → summary generation
features: Prepared review–TL;DR–summary sequences and a PyTorch training loop in the original coursework notebook.
Built a review-only evaluator that scores every batch item and compares against a lead-words baseline.
Measured a 513-review pilot with public pretrained GPT-2; published examples, settings, and limitations.
projects.notes: The original fine-tuned checkpoint is unavailable. The pilot evaluates public pretrained GPT-2, not the coursework model; the historical notebook scores are unreliable. ROUGE is an imperfect proxy and the sample is not independently reviewed or deduplicated.
highlights: Review-only evaluation covering 513 held-out reviews and a partial final batch.
Lead baseline ROUGE-L 0.097; pretrained GPT-2 0.049. Fine-tuned model not evaluated.

projects.name: C++ Concepts & Systems Lab
projects.summary: Interactive C++ lessons and a C++17 filesystem lab exploring containers, recursive operations, and concurrency.
projects.flow: Concepts: lesson → simulation or compiler-backed vector trace. Systems: sequential or bounded-worker copy → verified outputs and timings.
features: Created data-driven memory and container teaching simulations, clearly distinguished from actual program output.
Added an instrumented vector example that displays values, size and capacity printed by a real Wandbox run.
Built a bounded-worker file-copy experiment with a sequential mode and verified repeated benchmarks.
Implemented educational command classes for cd, ls, cp, mv, and rm; the original threaded commands remain separate.
projects.notes: The live vector example visualizes instrumented program output, not debugger or memory-address traces. The separate copy benchmark uses small synthetic workloads; the original Q3 commands still use unbounded threads. Compiler access requires Wandbox.
highlights: Interactive teaching simulations plus a live vector trace from compiler output.
Bounded-worker file copy, tested against a sequential mode on repeatable workloads.
